question.worked_solution:
The chain rule in vector form states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))]=∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t).
$$

In addition, we've been given that

$$
∇f(x,y)=(\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+y)+\frac{x}{x+y})i+\frac{x}{x+y}\,j.
$$

First, we substitute $x=2t$ and $y=1-2t$ into $∇f(x,y)$ to find $∇f(r(t)):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(r(t)) & =(\operatorname{ln}⁡(2t+1-2t)+\frac{2t}{2t+1-2t})i+\frac{2t}{2t+1-2t}\,j \\  & =2t\,i+2t\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the derivative of $r(t),$ which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1-2t)\,j \\  & =2\,i+(-2)\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))] & =∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) \\  & =(2t\,i+2t\,j)\cdot (2\,i+(-2)\,j) \\  & =2t\cdot 2+2t\cdot (-2) \\  & =4t-4t \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, evaluating the above at $t=\sqrt{2},$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(\sqrt{2}))] & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
